title: a 4:4:4 frame clears 16 bytes per superblock column of a uv context carved for 4:2:0's 8
consumer: libavcodec/vp9.c:3877-3878 at the fix's parent, vp9_decode_frame()
object: the update_size() block, one av_malloc(sb_cols * (240 + sizeof(lflvl) + 16 * sizeof(mv))) at libavcodec/vp9.c:329, carved by assign() at :331-347
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the block is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: a region sized for one chroma subsampling and written for another
allocator_layer: FFmpeg's own carve of one allocation: the block is the platform's calloc/malloc (as in ../plain-heap-repros, so the allocation bound the arms enforce is real and exact), and the regions are pointer arithmetic on it, exactly as upstream writes it, through shared/driver.c's ffc_carve().
fidelity: real carve arithmetic, model consumer. The block size and every region offset are upstream's expressions at the fix's parent, evaluated at the parameters named in case.c; the consumer is reduced to the stores or loads that cross, the first crossing access going through the labelled probe and the rest of the unreduced overshoot recorded as `extent`. The fixed arm models the fix's own change, including any change to the allocation.
nested_why: the crossed region was carved out of one allocation by FFmpeg's own pointer arithmetic, and the case CHECKs that the whole unreduced overshoot stays inside that allocation, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- the object is FFmpeg's carve, one layer inside malloc: NESTED.
